npcs.name: Lord-Commander Edric Ashdown
npcs.description: A tall, iron-grey man of sixty in plain black, with a soldier's straight back and a face that has not smiled in public for a decade. He wears no armour at all, as if he has decided he no longer has the right.
npcs.personality: Proud, exhausted, rigidly honourable, and sure that honour is what failed him. Believes the Order broke its oath at Greyford and that forsworn men should not ride. Loves his son and has never once said so. Underneath the iron, a man desperate for a reason to be wrong.
npcs.speech: Formal, clipped, old-fashioned. Calls people by rank or 'traveller'. Long silences instead of anger. When moved, his sentences get shorter, not longer.
npcs.greeting: 'Traveller. You have come a long way to look at a tomb. Say what you came to say.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the Order of Ash
topics.text: 'Four hundred years ago King Aldric knelt at that stone and swore the first of us to the crown. Hold where you are set. Never leave the crown alone in the dark.' He looks toward the chapel. 'Twelve years ago we left it. We are what is left of men who ran.'

topics.prompt: Ask what happened at Greyford
topics.text: 'The reavers came to the ford. We held it, as we were set to. Then the retreat horn sounded from the tower, and we obeyed it, because it was ours. Ser Halvard and nine others did not. They held the ford alone until they died, and while they died the reavers crossed upstream and burned Tarrow.' A silence. 'No order was ever sent. The Lord Marshal swore it before the Queen herself.'

topics.prompt: Ask who sounded the horn
topics.text: His jaw works. 'A knight of seventeen, set at the horn-post as an honour. He said a courier came in the Marshal's colours. No courier was ever found.' Edric looks at nothing. 'I took his spurs with my own hands. He was my son. He is my son. I do not speak of him.'

topics.prompt: Ask him to look at Corin
topics.text: Edric looks past you at his son for the space of a breath. Corin stands very straight and does not look away. Neither of them says a word, and then Edric turns back to you. 'You keep strange company, traveller.' His hand, on the table, has closed into a fist.

topics.prompt: Tell him the Regent has the heart-stone
topics.text: For a moment the iron goes out of him. 'Varric Caul.' He says the name as if it tastes of ash. 'He was Lord Marshal of the North, then. It was his oath against my son's.' He straightens. 'It changes nothing. Forsworn men do not get to choose which oath they keep.'

topics.prompt: Ask him to ride against the Regent
topics.text: Edric hears you out without moving.

topics.prompt: Lay the Greyford satchel before the Order
topics.text: 'The chapel, then,' Edric says, when he has seen what you carry. 'If a thing is to be said about the oath, it is said in front of the stone.'

topics.prompt: Ask what the Order will do now
topics.text: 'Mend saddles. Sharpen what has rusted. Write to every knight who left and tell them the stone has called.' He almost smiles. 'And when you go east to Highspire, traveller, you will not go alone.'

npcs.name: Knight-Sergeant Tamsin Reed
npcs.description: A square, weathered woman in mended mail, with dark braids pinned tight under her coif and a crossbow on her back that she clearly built herself.
npcs.personality: Blunt, practical, impatient with grief that has gone on too long. Was a squire at Greyford beside Corin and never believed he panicked. Wants the Order to ride and is tired of being the only one who says so.
npcs.speech: Short, salty sergeant's talk. Swears mildly and often. Calls Corin 'the boy' though he is nearly thirty and a head taller.
npcs.greeting: 'Another petitioner. Good. Maybe you'll be the one who kicks him.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the Lord-Commander
topics.text: 'Best knight I ever served. Twelve years now he's been holding a funeral for us.' She spits. 'He thinks if he makes the Order small enough and sad enough, it'll be punishment enough. It's not penance if nobody gets anything out of it.'

topics.prompt: Ask what she saw at Greyford
topics.text: 'I was sixteen, on the line. Heard the horn, turned my horse, like everyone.' Her mouth tightens. 'Corin was up in that tower. Two minutes after it sounded, the tower was on fire. Not reaver fire; they never got near it. Nobody ever asked who lit it.'

topics.prompt: Ask whether anyone searched the Horn Tower
topics.text: 'The Marshal's men went over the field. The Lord-Commander forbade any of us to go near the tower after. Said it was a place of shame.' She looks at you. 'Cellar's still under all those beams, if anyone wanted to get their hands dirty. I've been told not to.'

topics.prompt: Ask about Corin
topics.text: 'The boy? Still alive, still carrying water for refugees at the Last Lamp, still too stubborn to come home.' Gruff. 'He was the best of us at seventeen. Tell him Tam says he's an idiot. He'll know what it means.'

topics.prompt: Ask whether she would ride if the Order did
topics.text: 'I'd ride if it was me and the cook.' She pats the crossbow. 'But it won't be me and the cook. It'll be all of them or none of them, and that's down to him.'

npcs.name: Mother Hesk
npcs.description: A tiny, very old woman in three shawls, with hands like tree roots and a voice that can be heard from one end of the camp to the other. A kettle is always on near her.
npcs.personality: Unsentimental, tireless, fond of everyone and impressed by no one. Keeps a hundred refugees alive by sheer bossiness. Grieves at night where nobody can see.
npcs.speech: Northern, plain, a little scolding. Calls everyone 'pet'. Gives orders as questions: 'You'll be carrying that, won't you?'
npcs.greeting: 'Sit down before you fall down, pet. There's tea. It's terrible. Drink it.'

topics.prompt: Ask what is happening in the north
topics.text: 'The briars come in the night. Not fast. You wake up and they're over the well, and next night they're over the door, and you go, or you stay and stop feeling the cold.' She stirs the kettle. 'We went. A lot didn't.'

topics.prompt: Ask how the camp manages
topics.text: 'Badly, and all together.' She jerks a thumb at the full water barrels. 'And there's a great soft lad at the Last Lamp who carries our water every morning before light and runs off if anyone tries to say thank you. Knight, once. Won't say what happened.'

topics.prompt: Ask for some of her tea for the road
topics.text: 'Didn't I say it was terrible?' She fills a flask anyway. 'Bring the flask back.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the woman in the briars
topics.text: Hesk is quiet a long time. 'My sister saw her. In the snow past the mountains, wearing thorns like a crown. Said she looked right at her, and she was crying, and the briar stopped.' She shrugs, too sharply. 'My sister also saw a fish with a man's face once. Drink your tea.'

topics.prompt: Tell her the children are safe
topics.text: Hesk gets up, which she does not often do, and puts both root-hard hands on your face. 'Thank you, pet.' Then she turns and shouts for someone to heat water for baths, and does not look at you again until her eyes have dried.

npcs.name: Wenna
npcs.description: A lean young woman of about twenty with a soot-black face and forearms like a smith's, raking a charcoal clamp at the edge of the camp. She does not stop working to look at you.
npcs.personality: Hard, wary, angry in the slow way that has had years to set. The last of Tarrow's families left alive; she was nine. Hates the Order and the man who blew the horn. Kind to the camp's small children in a gruff, unbending way.
npcs.speech: Few words, flat, no softening. Doesn't use names. Says 'the knight' and 'the horn' as if they were swear words.
npcs.greeting: 'If you're with the knights, keep walking.'

topics.prompt: Ask where she is from
topics.text: 'Tarrow.' She rakes the coals. 'Forty-one people. I was under the mill floor with my mam's hand over my mouth. Then I wasn't, because she went to look.' A spark lands on her arm; she doesn't brush it off. 'You'll want to know if I blame anyone. Yes.'

topics.prompt: Ask what she thinks of the knight at the Last Lamp
topics.text: 'He carries water. He chalks the names. He thinks if he does it long enough it'll count.' She stabs the clamp. 'It doesn't count. They're still dead.'

topics.prompt: Ask her to come to Tarrow for the bell
topics.text: Wenna stops raking. It is the first time you have seen her hands still. 'The bell. Mam used to sing under it on feast days, louder than anyone.' A long breath. 'I'll come. Not for him. For them. And if he says one word to me, I'm walking back.'
topics.fail_text: 'No.' Flat. 'He can hang it and ring it and chalk his names. I'm not standing next to him while he does it.' She goes back to her coals. Maybe, if you knew more about that night, she would listen.

topics.prompt: Tell her the truth about Greyford and ask her to come for the bell
topics.text: She listens to the whole of it with the rake held still. 'A forged order.' She laughs, short and ugly, then not ugly at all. 'Twelve years I hated a boy for doing what he was told.' She wipes her face and leaves a clean stripe through the soot. 'I'll come and ring Mam's bell.'

npcs.name: Oswin Pell
npcs.description: A round, bald, cheerful man in a leather apron, with a lantern hook on his belt and a scorch mark on every sleeve. He looks like he has not slept since the refugees started coming, and like he does not mind.
npcs.personality: Warm, gossipy, endlessly hospitable, quietly brave. Keeps every lamp lit because his grandfather swore to the Order that he would. Fond of Corin like a stray dog that turned out to be a wolfhound.
npcs.speech: Rambling, friendly, full of 'now then' and 'bless you'. Drifts into stories and drifts back.
npcs.greeting: 'Now then! Come in, come in, there's a fire, there's soup, there's a bench with only one bad leg.'

topics.prompt: Ask why every lamp is lit
topics.text: 'My grandfather kept this place for the Order's riders. Swore a lamp would always burn in the Marches for anyone on the road.' He trims a wick. 'Order doesn't ride any more. Road's busier than it ever was. So.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the big man splitting wood
topics.text: 'Corin? Bless him. Turned up nine winters back with a horse that died the week after and a sword he wouldn't sell. Works for his bed and won't take coin.' Oswin lowers his voice. 'Used to be a knight. Don't call him Sir. He goes very quiet.'

topics.prompt: Tell him the hounds on the road are dead
topics.text: 'Dead? All of them?' Oswin sits down on his bad bench, which promptly tips him off it. From the floor: 'Bless you. Bless you. I'll stop sending the children the long way round.'

npcs.name: Brother Lark
npcs.description: A thin young person in a robe stitched all over with thorns, bare-footed in the snow, with frost in their eyelashes and a face that would be gentle if it were not so empty.
npcs.personality: Soft-spoken, sincere, and certain. Was the acolyte at Tarrow's chapel and watched it burn at fourteen. Has decided that cold is kinder than fire, because nobody screams in the cold. Not cruel; terribly kind in the wrong direction.
npcs.speech: Quiet, sing-song, always gentle. Speaks of the Thornwake as 'the hush' and the Thorn Queen as 'our Lady'.
npcs.greeting: 'Hush. Sit. You've walked so far. You don't have to be cold any more, you know. Nobody does.'

topics.prompt: Ask what the Choir believes
topics.text: 'The world burns. It always has. Kings, wars, fevers, fire.' They smile at you with great tenderness. 'The hush doesn't burn. It only holds. Our Lady in the north holds back the end of everything with her own two arms, and she's not afraid any more, and neither are we.'

topics.prompt: Ask who their Lady is
topics.text: 'She wears the briar like a crown. She walked into the north so the rest of us wouldn't have to.' Lark's frosted lashes flutter. 'Some say she was a queen once. I think she was just a mother who loved everyone too much.'

topics.prompt: Ask how they are, now
topics.text: Lark is sitting by one of Cinderfold's fires in a borrowed coat, their thorn-stitched robe folded small beside them. 'Cold,' they say, and laugh, a little shakily. 'It hurts. I'd forgotten it was supposed to.' They hold their hands out to the flames. 'Thank you for making it hurt.'

topics.prompt: Ask whether they knew Tarrow
topics.text: Something moves under the calm, like a fish under ice. 'I rang the bell there. On feast days.' The smile stays exactly where it is. 'It was very loud, that night. Everything was. Hush now.'
